notes:
Launching a big fleet no longer takes the machine down. Starting a lot of accounts at once could use up all the memory on the machine and lock it up completely - on a rented VPS especially - and the only way out was a hard power off, which is the one thing most likely to damage your data. Raising the delay between launches did not help, because that delay only changes how quickly the bots start, not how much memory they need once they are all running. OPTiC now checks the free memory before each launch and stops the queue when there is not enough left, telling you how many started and how much was free instead of freezing. Set the level under Bots, Automation, Stop launching below - or put it at 0 to turn the check off.
A web page can no longer reach OPTiC behind your back. OPTiC listens on your own machine so your bots can talk to it. Until now, any web page you happened to have open could quietly send it instructions that your browser would carry out - including changing your settings - and could read what OPTiC sent back. Those requests are now refused, and OPTiC's replies can no longer be read from another site. Nothing about the way your bots talk to OPTiC changes.
See an account's alliance without leaving the Bots page. The alliance shows in a small tag beside the account name, and as its own column if you would rather have it there. Turn it on or off from the Columns button like any other column.
The Scripts page matches the rest of the app. Same cards and the same spacing as the Tools page. It was the last page still on the old layout.
Faster on installs with a lot of history. Two lookups that run on every report your bots send were reading through an entire table each time, which gets slower the more you have stored. Both are indexed now, so reports are processed quicker and the app stays responsive while a big fleet is reporting in.
